title: [YouPass Collect] - Computer ownership in the US from 1997 to 2012
prompt: The chart below gives information about computer ownership per household in the US from 1997 to 2012. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line chart compares changes in the percentages of Americans with different numbers of computers in the US from 1997 to 2012.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, computers became more prevalent in Americans over the given period. In addition, at the start of the period, the majority did not own a computer, while by the end of it, most owned at least one computer.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the graph in more detail, in 1997, nearly 70% of the US population did not have access to a computer at home, while around 28% had just one. Thereafter, the percentage of Americans with only one computer doubled to around 50% in 2003 before remaining at roughly that level until the end of the period. By contrast, there was a corresponding drop in the percentage of individuals in the US without computers, finishing the period at just under 20%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to groups with 2 or more computers, in the beginning, only 5% of US residents owned 2 computers, and almost none had three or more. In the following years, those with just 2 computers saw a rise in prevalence, increasing gradually to over a fifth at the end of the period. Likewise, there was also an upward trend in the proportion of individuals with three or more computers to around 10% in 2006, followed by relatively little change for the rest of the period.
